scope: Physical pages166/167 only. Figure127 observations come exclusively from the single full-page166 opening and are preparation for a later RAW review, not crop/SVG approval.

objects.observation: At the top is a thick, essentially horizontal aerial stroke, with a left arm and a right arm meeting at a central upright. A small central bump is visible at the junction. There is no arrowhead, length annotation or printed polarization vector.
A slender upright descends from the aerial midpoint toward the roof. It reaches a small peaked support above the roof; visible central strokes continue into the roof region.
relations: joins the aerial near its midpoint
is above and enters the roof/support region

objects.observation: Oblique strokes spread down-left and down-right around the upright, forming a small A-like/peaked support at the roof top. Short interior strokes are visible inside this support. These visible strokes must be retained; no hidden fastening or electrical junction is inferred.

The roof is an irregular side-view outline: its upper-left boundary climbs obliquely from the left eave to a higher corner, then runs almost horizontally rightward. The right boundary descends to the eave. The lower roof edge runs nearly horizontally. This is not a complete symmetric gable or rectangular grid.
relations: below the aerial and peaked support

objects.observation: The roof area contains repeated dark upright strips separated by narrow pale upright channels. Their upper ends follow the rising left boundary and then the flat upper boundary; their lower ends follow the eave. Speckled interruptions remain in some dark areas. These are visible roofing strokes, not calibrated cells or stated engineering dimensions.
objects.countPolicy: No exact strip/channel count is asserted from this full-page-only observation. The later RAW reviewer must compare the actual crop and preserve the printed strokes, without replacing them with an invented lattice.

objects.observation: Closely spaced, nearly horizontal parallel edge strokes run below the roof from the left overhang to the right edge. They form a narrow eave band, including a heavy upper edge and thinner lower boundary.
relations: separates the roof from the facade
crossed by the descending central lead-like stroke

objects.observation: A long vertical wall-edge stroke descends from near the left eave. The lower building is a partial elevation, not a closed house outline; no ground line or full wall rectangle is printed.

A dark descending stroke continues from the central roof region through the eave, bends leftward under the eave and then turns down toward the upper-right area of the left window group. It has visible bends rather than being a straight generic mast extension.
relations: approaches the upper-right part of the left window drawing
objects.limit: The visible route is recorded. A hidden receiver, exact electrical terminal and electrical connectivity at obscured intersections are not asserted.

objects.observation: The left main window-like group has a short top horizontal edge, long side strokes, multiple close horizontal crossbars near its top and short/long vertical interior divisions. Several lower strokes terminate separately; the lower frame is not closed. The descending lead-like stroke meets or approaches its upper-right area.

The middle main window-like group is separate from the left one. It has a top horizontal edge, long outer/inner side strokes, close horizontal crossbars and short upper plus longer lower vertical divisions. Its bottom is also unfinished/open in the printed drawing.

At the far right a third, partial window/facade group shows a vertical edge, a short top edge, short rightward crossbars and interrupted lower vertical strokes. It must remain partial; completing a third full window or a hidden building side would add source content.

figures.adjacentText: The question3 ending is above the aerial. The separate 图127 caption is below the drawing. Question4 begins below that caption. Their page-level separation is visible; this does not certify the crop margin.

pages.layout: Widely spaced large 光学 chapter heading, separate 引言 heading and a parenthetical subtitle; four prose paragraphs of5/4/3/4 rows; dotted italic157 footer at the lower right. The last paragraph is open at 沿着.

glyphs.observation: The second glyph is complex, with an additional dense upper component and lower component, not the simple two-part 须. The actual full-page pixels support retaining 鬚; the first glyph supports 触.
The second occurrence independently shows the same complex 鬚 structure. The frozen spelling 触鬚 is supported, not accepted from the author's crop assertion.

typography.observation: The nine-character lead-in is visibly heavy, contrasting with the ordinary serif continuation beginning 光从光源. The existing strong span matches that distinction.

There are repeated lower dot-like marks in the vicinity of 传送物质 and 改变物体间媒 on row14, and a particularly aligned sequence beneath 质的状态 on row15. Their attribution as printed emphasis and their complete span are not established well enough here to approve omission or invent an equivalent strong span.
